methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
AMP Robotics is a Series A-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Matanya Horowitz that has raised $439.1M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), with peer assessments anchored to companies including Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics spanning seed through Series B stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $30M total-raised proxy as a base and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $60M. Peer-median analysis across the four same-sector comparables produces a $1.7B midpoint, with observed range of $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B).

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $51M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $880M. The substantial spread reflects stage and funding variance within the peer set; peers at Series B command 20–100x higher valuations than early-stage equivalents. Key uncertainties include the timing and terms of AMP's next funding round relative to peer trajectory, and whether the $439.1M raised positions the company materially ahead of or behind peer capital efficiency benchmarks. The median estimate is most reliable where peer staging clusters most tightly, though applicability of the $1.7B peer median to an ostensibly earlier-stage target warrants downside consideration.
